items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 14, 2026
items.excerpt: Merve Aydogan 14 November 2026• Update: 14 November 2026 HAMILTON, Canada Here's a rundown of all the news you need to know for Saturday, including Türkiye and Qatar signing five agreements, including a mutual defense pact, during the 12th meeting of the Türkiye-Qatar High Strategic Committee in Istanbul; the US Federal Aviation Administration lifting a nationwide flight ground stop after a telecommunications outage; and US President Donald Trump set to hold trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen next week, according to the White House. Türkiye and Qatar signed five agreements, including a mutual defense pact, during the 12th meeting of the Türkiye-Qatar High Strategic Committee in Istanbul, with the signing ceremony held at the Presidential Dolmabahce Office in the presence of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. Erdogan and Sheikh Tamim signed the mutual defense agreement, while the other deals cover consumer protection, education, and cooperation on peace, reconciliation and conflict resolution. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani signed the memorandum on peace, reconciliation and conflict resolution, along with a joint declaration marking the committee’s 12th meeting. - US FAA lifts nationwide flight ground stop after telecommunications outage The US Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop at airports after a telecommunications outage affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers prompted authorities to halt flights as a precaution, with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy describing the problem as a "communication issue" and "an emergency." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that the public was "never" in danger and that there was "no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack." "We’re not ruling out anything," Mullin said when asked about a possible cyberattack, while the FAA said every flight had been accounted for and international flights would be handled case by case. Separately, Microsoft said it had "no indication" the ground stop was related to any of its services, while FlightAware said more than 10,000 flights were delayed or canceled. - Trump to hold trilateral talks with Xi, Putin in China next week: White House US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, with assistant White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales saying he will discuss reducing nuclear weapons, whose proliferation Trump believes is "very dangerous." A senior US official said Washington does not expect an agreement, calling the talks "the entry point, the first conversation" at the leader level, and said Trump plans to raise Iran but not Ukraine because China is not part of the separate US-Russia track. Trump will leave Washington on Monday for Manila for a Quad leaders’ meeting and the US-ASEAN Special Summit, then travel to Shenzhen on Wednesday, where he will hold a meeting and working lunch with Xi on Thursday before the trilateral meeting. Another senior US official described the Trump-Xi session as an "implementation check-in” on the trade agreement, with no tariff changes expected. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk will join Trump for parts of his visit to China but will not participate in official meetings, according to US officials. ... - ... - The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the US measles elimination status after outbreaks in several states and 5,400 cases reported in 2026, with health experts blaming low vaccination coverage.

items.title: Morning Digest: All departing U.S. flights grounded due to communication outage; Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide, India feels impact, and more - The Hindu
items.excerpt: #### All departing U.S. flights grounded due to communication outage All flights in the U.S. were grounded on Friday (November 13, 2026), sparking travel chaos across the vast country, after what government officials said was a major communications outage, insisting it was not the result of any “nefarious attack.” The nationwide stop left tens of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events. The incident marked only the second time such an alert was given in U.S. airspace since the 9/11 attacks. #### Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which began on Thursday (November 12, 2026) and continued late into Friday (November 13, 2026), affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations. In its latest update on Friday (November 13, 2026), the company said it was making progress in fixing the outage, which has affected email access and workplace applications in businesses, public services, and other organisations across the globe. In India, the disruptions affected businesses from startups to multinational corporations. Follow LIVE updates here. #### Tanker hits a river cruise boat on Mississippi River in New Orleans; rescue operations under way A tanker in New Orleans that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with 180 people aboard on Friday (November 13, 2026), the Mayor said. All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River as the ship took on water and began to topple over. Video from the scene showed the much larger Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the cruise boat while it was docked as metal and glass crashed and crunched. #### In major breakthrough, U.S. assures India of comparative tariff advantage over its competitors In a significant breakthrough towards the conclusion of the India-U.S. interim deal on trade, the U.S. has assured India of a comparative advantage over its competitors once it finalises its tariff structure, a senior official in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry said, adding that both sides are working to complete the deal by the end of the current financial year. Indian officials have repeatedly been saying that India would move ahead with a deal only if the U.S. assured it of a comparative advantage, as was agreed to in the February 2026 joint statement between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump. ... #### Students among 24 dead in bus-truck collision in Assam’s Kaziranga College students were among 24 people killed when a minibus collided head-on with a container truck at Rangajan near Kaziranga National Park in eastern Assam’s Golaghat district on Friday (November 13, 2026).

Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state lawmaker, defeated three Republicans. One of those, Bernadette Wilson, was endorsed by President Donald Trump. Kreiss-Tomkins’ victory is part of a national landslide that gave Democrats sweeping wins in state governments across the country. They now control 30 governor’s offices. Kreiss-Tomkins focused on issues including affordability and full funding of public schools. He emphasized his willingness to work across party lines and said Alaska needed a change in direction. ... TORONTO (AP) — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada and the U.S. are making progress on a trade deal after talks collapsed in August. Carney was in the Philippine capital on Saturday ahead of a key three-day summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and their Asian and Western counterparts. He says he spoke with President Donald Trump and senior officials before leaving for Europe and Asia. His aim is to reduce Canada's reliance on the U.S. amid Trump's trade war. Canada suspended negotiations in August due to U.S. demands. The countries have resumed discussions, with a focus on reducing tariffs on key sectors like steel and aluminum. ... ANTALYA, Turkey (AP) — United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres says the world must immediately and drastically cut fossil fuel emissions to avert the most catastrophic effects of climate change. Speaking to reporters Friday at the U.N.'s climate summit in Turkey, he said global warming contributes to geopolitical instability by driving hunger and displacement, pushing countries into debt and fueling competition for land and water. He urged the world to “follow the science” and face hard facts. “You cannot build peace on a burning planet,” he said. World leaders are trying to reach consensus on actions to address climate change and help vulnerable countries.

items.title: Bessent, Fed’s Goolsbee divided on role of energy shock in inflation By Reuters
items.excerpt: Published Nov 13, 2026, 09:02 AM ... WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday that the Federal Reserve should not hike rates because of inflation driven by an "energy supply shock" tied to the Iran war, comments made to CNBC and promptly contradicted on the network by Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, who said price pressures were building far beyond what could be explained by high oil prices. "I think the Fed should understand that this is an energy supply shock," while the underlying US economy is very strong, Bessent said in an interview on CNBC. "So I think that to hike too much into an energy supply shock when it’s coming down, these are very noisy numbers...You know, the Fed’s supposed to look into the future, not look in the rearview mirror." Shortly afterwards, the network hosted Goolsbee, a regular guest on CNBC’s morning Squawk Box show, who said that inflation was not just due to energy, but had spread to the service sector and areas like medical care that are not usually responsive to the price of oil, and was also elevated through strong demand tied to the AI data center buildout. "I respect the secretary and I am trying to figure out the same thing he is trying to figure out, which is how persistent is this inflation? The tariff inflation and oil price shock were supposed to have gone away by now and it hasn’t," Goolsbee said. "One puzzle is why have those supply shocks been as persistent as they have been. A second thing is if demand is overheating and that is contributing to inflation, that is more worrisome... Services inflation, which is probably not coming from tariffs or oil, is one of the more troubling aspects of the inflation reports we have been getting." While not committing to a rate hike, he said the Fed "has definitely got work to do to continue to reestablish its credibility." ... Research meanwhile opened a different window on the relationship between oil prices and US inflation. Because the US is an energy exporter, higher global oil prices can filter through to the economy in the form of higher corporate profits and wages, providing a source of inflation beyond supply issues that can’t be easily ignored by the central bank. Recent stronger-than-expected jobs and inflation reports have further bolstered the case for more ... "We have had signs of trouble now for several months in a row if you look at how broad-based the inflation is," Goolsbee said. "In categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you are still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way ...

items.title: The Fed chief said AI would tame inflation. His colleagues disagree. – DNYUZ
items.excerpt: November 14, 2026 in News When President Donald Trump chose him to lead the Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh argued that the artificial intelligence boom would help tame inflation. More than a dozen of his colleagues, including two other Trump appointees, now say it’s doing the opposite, playing a role in fueling inflation, which could soon mean even higher interest rates on credit cards, car loans and mortgages. Warsh will get a chance to revisit that argument on Monday, when he opens a conference in San Francisco meant to inform the work of a task force he created to study AI’s effects on jobs and productivity. He heads into it looking increasingly out of step with many other Fed officials. This week, Fed governor Michelle Bowman, a Trump appointee who like Warsh once predicted AI would help push inflation down, conceded that is not yet happening. She said the AI buildout accounts for roughly a quarter of the excess inflation the Fed is fighting, about as much as the pressure from tariffs or energy prices. Fed governor Christopher Waller, who said a big interest rate hike should be on the table in December, on Tuesday pointed to research by Fed economists on AI and high energy prices. Their findings, the Trump appointee said, “do not encourage me to think that these factors will be fading anytime soon.” Hotter-than-expected inflation numbers out this week underscored the concerns raised by Bowman and Waller. Electricity prices jumped in October, and smartphones also logged their largest monthly increase since the government began tracking them separately in 2019. The data center buildout has been driving up electricity prices over the past year, as well as demand for chips that are also critical for consumer electronics. Warsh has acknowledged that the artificial intelligence boom is increasing the price of computer chips, but he has questioned whether it is driving inflation more broadly. “Economic growth is higher, but that doesn’t tell me that economic growth is somehow causing inflation and making our job harder,” he said at his news conference last month after the Fed held rates steady a week before the midterm elections. Warsh said politics played no role in the decision. The debate over AI’s role in inflation comes down to timing. Right now companies racing to build AI are competing for the same chips, electricity and electricians, which pushes prices up. But AI could eventually make businesses more efficient, allowing them to produce more for less and helping hold prices down. If that payoff comes in the near term, as Warsh suggested before he took over the Federal Reserve, the central bank can afford to be patient. If the productivity gains are years away, as many at the Fed now fear, Fed officials may need to keep raising interest rates to cool things off. So far, Warsh’s views haven’t kept the Fed from acting. The Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously to raise rates in September for the first time in more than three years. Several officials have said they expect another increase at the Fed’s December meeting.

items.title: Democrats turn to 2028 after midterm gains boost moderates and progressives | U.S. | EL PAÍS English
items.excerpt: Luis Doncel New York - Nov 14, 2026 - 05:00 CET Ten days have passed since Democrats delivered one of the most consequential midterm victories in modern U.S. history. The scale of the Republican defeat has drawn comparisons to the post-Watergate elections of the 1970s. But for Democrats, the harder task begins now: converting an electoral backlash against Donald Trump into a durable political project. They achieved their main objective, but the hard part starts now. Their most important challenge will be convincing voters who turned their backs on the party of Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Kamala Harris that a new generation of leaders has answers to the problems they face in their daily lives. Looking ahead to the 2028 presidential election, Democrats will have to organize internally, decide what policies to offer and, above all, determine which wing of the party will take the lead: establishment centrists, such as Hakeem Jeffries, the likely next Speaker of the House, or progressives led by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. Two things seem certain. First, the top priority is bringing soaring prices under control. The high cost of gasoline, housing, food, healthcare and virtually every other necessity of daily life helps explain election results that Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described as “close to an extinction-level event for Republicans.” ... The challenge, however, is that Donald Trump will remain in the White House for another two years and has threatened to veto any major legislation emerging from Congress. It is also unclear who would reap the political benefits of any improvement in Americans’ quality of life ahead of 2028: the president’s party, or the Democrats, who emerged from the midterms with control of both chambers. “The American people don’t want us to get even. They want us to get things done on their behalf. We ran on affordability. We won on affordability. And now it’s our job to govern on affordability,” Jeffries said Thursday on Morning Joe. That view is widely shared within the party. ## Little interest in impeachment A second lesson from the midterm election is that Democrats have little interest in pursuing impeachment proceedings against Trump. Such an effort would consume enormous political energy and, as previous attempts demonstrated, is unlikely to produce the desired outcome. Rather than removing the president from office, it could once again provide him with a powerful platform. Democrats are equally reluctant to refight the culture-war battles over transgender rights and other identity issues that conservatives have so effectively weaponized in recent years. Perhaps no one has captured the party’s mood more clearly than Gina Hinojosa, the governor-elect of Texas: “The left-right paradigm just does not meet the moment of our time,” she said. “This is about 99.9% of us in the same boat against 15 billionaire tech guys who are frankly controlling government. And that’s what the people voted against in this election [...] And we didn’t just have Democrat supporters, we had independent supporters and Republican supporters.” ... Dave Hopkins, a political science professor at Boston College, sees a similar dynamic at work. In a video call, he argues that over the past decade Democrats have paid a steep political price for culture-war battles, which have undermined the party’s appeal among working-class voters, including members of minority groups such as Black and Latino Americans. “There is a consensus among the party’s factions that they now have to focus on the economy and equal opportunity,” said Hopkins, whose latest book, Polarized by Degrees, examines how the educational gap and the culture war have transformed U.S. politics. “The problem is that the recipe for achieving that improvement varies greatly depending on which leaders propose it.” ... The internal battle has not yet begun, but few doubt that it will ... Centrists have taken comfort from the scale of the party’s victory in the House of Representatives. With only a handful of races still to be called, Democrats already hold 255 seats, with female lawmakers in the party surpassing 100 for the first time. That gives the Democrats a sizable cushion above the 218 seats required for a majority, making it difficult for the party’s left flank to use the threat of defections as leverage in internal negotiations. As a result, the scenes of dysfunction that frequently marked the past two years, when Republicans controlled the House by just four seats, are unlikely to be repeated.

Kreiss-Tomkins’ victory is part of a national landslide that gave Democrats sweeping wins in state governments across the country. They now control 30 governor’s offices. Kreiss-Tomkins focused on issues including affordability and full funding of public schools. He emphasized his willingness to work across party lines and said Alaska needed a change in direction. JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — Alaska voters have rejected a ballot measure seeking to repeal the state’s unique system of open primaries and ranked choice voting in general elections. Voters during the Nov. 3 election were asked for the second time in two years whether to repeal the system and certain campaign disclosure rules. They narrowly approved adopting the system in 2020, and it was used for the first time two years later. Supporters of open primaries and ranked voting say it invites competition and gives voters more choices. Opponents, including President Donald Trump, say it’s confusing. WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump has been all over the map as he's articulated his thinking about the Iran war since last week's midterm elections. He's backed away from additional strikes on Iran — but also from additional talks. On Monday, Trump suggested the war was partly to blame for Republican losses and said the conflict "militarily is effectively over." By Thursday, he dismissed the need for a deal with Iran, redirecting Vice President JD Vance to focus on domestic issues. Trump's shifting tone adds uncertainty to the conflict's future. Meanwhile, U.S. officials say the decision on how to proceed rests with Trump, who remains confident in his economic strategy against Iran. TORONTO (AP) — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada and the U.S. are making progress on a trade deal after talks collapsed in August.

items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 14, 2026
items.excerpt: - US FAA lifts nationwide flight ground stop after telecommunications outage The US Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop at airports after a telecommunications outage affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers prompted authorities to halt flights as a precaution, with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy describing the problem as a "communication issue" and "an emergency." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that the public was "never" in danger and that there was "no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack." "We’re not ruling out anything," Mullin said when asked about a possible cyberattack, while the FAA said every flight had been accounted for and international flights would be handled case by case. Separately, Microsoft said it had "no indication" the ground stop was related to any of its services, while FlightAware said more than 10,000 flights were delayed or canceled. - Trump to hold trilateral talks with Xi, Putin in China next week: White House US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, with assistant White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales saying he will discuss reducing nuclear weapons, whose proliferation Trump believes is "very dangerous." A senior US official said Washington does not expect an agreement, calling the talks "the entry point, the first conversation" at the leader level, and said Trump plans to raise Iran but not Ukraine because China is not part of the separate US-Russia track. Trump will leave Washington on Monday for Manila for a Quad leaders’ meeting and the US-ASEAN Special Summit, then travel to Shenzhen on Wednesday, where he will hold a meeting and working lunch with Xi on Thursday before the trilateral meeting. Another senior US official described the Trump-Xi session as an "implementation check-in” on the trade agreement, with no tariff changes expected. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk will join Trump for parts of his visit to China but will not participate in official meetings, according to US officials.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 14 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: ## Trailers and first looks Sony Pictures Classics has released the official US teaser trailer for Iron Boy, Louis Clichy’s hand-drawn animated feature and winner of the Special Jury Prize in Un Certain Regard at Cannes. The film opens in limited release on 4 December 2026, with a nationwide release on 22 January 2027. Keerthy Suresh plays Savithiri, a lawyer fighting to save her husband, in the trailer for Sathyavan Savithiri, out now ahead of the film’s 20 November 2026 theatrical release. Mysskin plays a major part. Bhuvan Bam is back as Titu Mama in the Dhindora season 2 trailer, with Sanjeeda Sheikh joining the cast as Kavita Mami. The new season premieres on Netflix on 20 November 2026. A young man who moves to Kathmandu to change his life after being unable to succeed in his studies is the subject of Gobar Ganesh, whose trailer is out. The Nepali film is directed by Marichman Shrestha and stars Balchhi and Barsha Siwakoti. It reaches cinemas on Magh 1. Dhiraaj Rajbanshi’s Himalayan Gold has a second trailer out, ahead of its 20 November 2026 cinema release. Sunil Thapa, Karma, Parikshya Limbu and Rahul Mukhia star. Dhanush and Mammootty share the screen for the first time in the OM: Chapter 1 trailer, out now. Rajkumar Periasamy directs, and the film opens in theatres worldwide on 20 November 2026. Christopher Briney and Michelle Randolph star in Clashing Through the Snow, whose first trailer is out. The holiday road-trip romantic comedy, directed by Carlson Young, premieres on Prime Video on 23 November 2026. The 1960 plot to assassinate Fidel Castro during his United Nations visit is the subject of Killing Castro, whose official trailer Lionsgate has released. Produced by Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson and DJ Khaled, it opens in cinemas on 11 December 2026 and arrives on digital on 18 December. D Gukesh, R Praggnanandhaa, R Vaishali, Arjun Erigaisi and Vidit Gujrathi are the subjects of CANDIDATES, a six-episode series whose official trailer Dopamine Media has released. It premieres on the Dopamine Media YouTube channel on 22 November 2026. ## Casting and production Cristiano Ronaldo has begun production on Day 1s, his first television show. The scripted drama follows a fictional elite football agency and comes from UR-Marv, with Ronaldo executive producing and expected to make his acting debut. No platform or release date has been announced. School Spirits has confirmed its season 4 cast, with 12 stars returning and one promoted to series regular. Christian Weissmann, Katharine Isabella, Clara Alexandrova and Briana Buckmaster join as guest stars, and production is under way. Vishwambhara, Chiranjeevi’s fantasy adventure known during production as Mega 156, has begun its regular shoot. The film is directed by Vassishta and produced by UV Creations, and is billed as the costliest film of Chiranjeevi’s career. Isla Fisher and Blake Ritson have joined Al Pacino in Captivated, Dito Montiel’s thriller about the kidnapping of John Paul Getty III, with Jackson Kelly also joining the cast. Production is under way in Calabria and Rome in Italy. Apple TV has promoted Samba Schutte to series regular for Pluribus season 2. His Mr. Diabate returns with an expanded presence after two guest episodes in season 1. No premiere date has been announced. Netflix has announced Pushpak Vimaan, a crime-caper comedy series from Sudip Sharma starring Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee and Barun Sobti. No premiere date was given with the announcement. Kai Cech is to voice Shanti in Lost in Mandala, the first global animated feature from Nepal’s Incessant Rain Studios. The film is directed by former Disney visual effects supervisor Kiran Bhakta Joshi, with a screenplay by Zack Stentz, and is now in pre-production with no release date announced. MobLand season 3 starts production next week. Helen Mirren confirmed the start on the A Talent for Murder red carpet, with Tom Hardy and Pierce Brosnan returning. The season 2 finale airs on 20 November 2026. Freya Allan is to lead System, a horror film from director Joachim Ronning. Filming is under way in abandoned London Underground stations and tunnels, with Denzel Baidoo and Felix Edwards co-starring. ## Box office and streaming Ramayana: Rise of a Legend has crossed $100 million worldwide in seven days, with Rs 944.55 crore reported by Sacnilk. CNBC TV18 reports it as the first film outside China to reach the mark in 2026. The Kannada dubbed version of Ramayana: Part 1 has crossed Rs 50 crore net in India, the first Bollywood film to do so. It took Rs 48.95 crore in its eight-day opening week plus Rs 1.17 crore on day 9, and the Karnataka gross across all languages has passed Rs 100 crore. Paper Tiger has debuted at 85 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 114 reviews. The James Gray crime drama stars Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson, and opened in limited release on 13 November 2026. Hulu has set 13 January 2027 as the premiere date for The Spot, an A24 psychological thriller starring Claire Danes and Ewan McGregor as a surgeon and her schoolteacher husband who suspect she caused a child’s hit-and-run death. First-look images were released on 12 November 2026.
